text.p: Holders Panathinaikos took a major step towards the next round of basketball's EuroLeague on Wednesday when they beat major rivals Barcelona 79-75 in front of a noisy 13,000-strong home crowd.

Panathinaikos, who beat Barcelona by a single basket in last season's controversial final, relied on explosive power forward Nikos Economou who penetrated the Spanish defence at will sinking 22 points in the group C encounter at Athens' Olympic Stadium.

The Greeks took a nine point lead midway through the first half but Barcelona recovered to lead 40-38 at halftime mainly through the efforts of Lithuanian Arturas Karnisovas who top-scored for the visitors with 17 points.

But Karnisovas played with four fouls in most of the second half, stripping Barcelona of fire power as the Greeks recovered and forced a steady 10 point lead until the last 30 seconds when the Spaniards notched five unanswered points.
German guard Michael Koch contributed 17 points for Panathinaikos and mercurial American playmaker Byron Dinkins added 16, including two triples.
Javier Fernandez and Roger Estejer sunk 11 points each for Barcelona.

The victory was a sweet revenge for Panathinaikos who suffered a humiliating 77-58 defeat in Spain two months ago and a personal win for Serb coach Bojidar Malkovic in an ongoing vendetta with Barcelona coach Aido Reneses.

The two men dislike of each other, they often exchange sarcastic remarks and never shake hands after the end of a match. In last season's final, Pananthinaikos edged home 67-66 but Barcelona lodged an objection, saying the Greeks had violated the 30 second shooting rule in the last minute.
The matter was eventually settled with international basketball federation FIBA offering "moral compensation" to the Spanish.
Wednesday's victory put the Greek club two points clear of Barcelona after seven matches.
